solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rings one's seen beyond void

indicators.note: something seen beyond another comes after it, so this piece follows the first

parts.note: to void a contract is to annul it, cancel it as invalid
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is the link to 'seen'

explanation.surface: Someone spots a ring through an empty space beyond.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of annulus, the Latin-derived word for a ring-shaped figure or part.

clue.text: Misrepresent female intuition

parts.note: to belie is to give a false impression of, to misrepresent

explanation.surface: A complaint that female intuition gets misrepresented.
explanation.definitionFit: An intuition is something held true without proof, a conviction or faith in it.

clue.text: Cash someone will come to get

definitions.text: Cash someone will come to get

parts.words: Cash someone will come to get
parts.note: reads like money waiting to be collected, but is the fee a star is paid simply for turning up at an event

explanation.surface: Money set aside for whoever comes to collect it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fee paid to a celebrity or athlete merely for attending an event, coming to it to get cash.

clue.text: Criticising materials used by roofer

definitions.meaning: harshly criticising them, a British informal sense

explanation.surface: A roofer's materials come in for criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a verb form meaning attacking harshly in print and a noun for slate roofing material.

clue.text: Privatising brings sale with indignation erupting

indicators.note: erupting suggests the letters burst out and land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A privatisation sell-off provokes an outburst of public anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erupting' scrambles the letters of SALE and INDIGNATION together; 'brings' and 'with' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Denationalising a state industry transfers it from public to private ownership, which is privatising it.

clue.text: Order apt to be blasted out by wolfish type

indicators.note: blasting something out scatters it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wolfish character issues a fitting order to blast something.
explanation.definitionFit: A wolf is a hunting animal, so a wolfish type is a predatory person or creature.

clue.text: The answer here probably has only one letter!

definitions.text: The answer here probably has only one letter!

parts.words: The answer here probably has only one letter!
parts.note: seems to be about the crossword answer's length, but a reply to a letter is posted in a single paper cover

explanation.surface: A joke that the answer is just one letter long.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper cover for posting mail usually holds a single letter, the reply sent inside.

clue.text: Peril not problematical for group seeking criminals

indicators.note: something problematical is in a mess, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Danger isn't a problem for a police force hunting criminals.
explanation.definitionFit: The international police organisation coordinating cross-border hunts for wanted criminals.

clue.text: Characters enthralled by worker ranting, deviating from the norm

indicators.note: Characters enthralled by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: People are captivated by an employee's rant against convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Errant means straying from the proper course, departing from accepted standards.

clue.text: Girl soon losing love

indicators.note: losing says a letter is dropped from the word before it

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon, shortly
love is zero in tennis scoring, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A girl is about to lose her love.
explanation.definitionFit: Ann is a girl's given name, an example of the class.

clue.text: Basic principle this person's found in harsh holy books

indicators.note: found in says this piece sits inside the other letters

parts.note: rude can mean harsh or rough, as in a rude awakening
this person is the speaker, I, and the 's is 'is', giving I'M
NT is the New Testament, a collection of holy books

explanation.surface: Someone claims to find a basic rule in severe scriptures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harsh' looks like describing the scriptures, but it gives its own piece; 'found in' places the speaker's contraction within that piece, before the holy books.
explanation.definitionFit: A rudiment is one of the first, most elementary principles of a subject.

clue.text: Theologian into drink, delivery initially confused

indicators.note: into puts the theologian inside the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink, beer
DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word delivery

explanation.surface: A theologian takes to drink and his sermon delivery becomes muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: Addled means muddled or confused, as in an addled brain.

clue.text: Something A-level maths student does to achieve distinction

definitions.meaning: calculus students find derivatives, a procedure; A-level is the British final school exam
telling things apart, recognising a difference between them

explanation.surface: A maths student works hard to get top grades.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the calculus operation of finding a derivative and the act of telling things apart.

clue.text: Parent not half thick

indicators.note: not half keeps only one half of the word, its first three letters

parts.note: a father is a parent

explanation.surface: A parent who is not half stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: Fat means thick or bulky, as in a fat book.

clue.text: Work is not bad, offering possibilities

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A job that isn't bad comes with choices.
explanation.definitionFit: Options are choices, things it is possible to choose between.

clue.text: Extend professional area

parts.note: pro is short for professional
a tract is an area of land

explanation.surface: An expert's patch of land gets bigger.
explanation.definitionFit: To protract is to prolong, drawing something out in time.

clue.text: Home if tiny unlikely to convey vastness

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: an unlikely form of the words is a rearranged one

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A tiny home is hardly likely to feel vast.
explanation.definitionFit: Infinity is boundless extent, endlessness, immeasurable space.

clue.text: Venus de Milo is so defenceless

definitions.meaning: the famous ancient statue has lost its arms
without weapons, unable to defend oneself

explanation.surface: The armless statue of Venus is left vulnerable.
explanation.definitionFit: Without weapons, and also playfully, without arms in the anatomical sense.

clue.text: Revolutionary order intercepted by a Communist leader

indicators.note: intercepted by says the order has another letter put into it
revolutionary means turned round, so the order is read backwards

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A revolutionary command is cut off by a Communist chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Chairman Mao Zedong led the Chinese Communist Party and the People's Republic.

clue.text: Taxi runs into horse — it's ghastly

indicators.note: into puts the taxi and runs inside the horse

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A cab ploughs into a horse, a gruesome sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Macabre means gruesome, dwelling on death and horror.

clue.text: Volume set aside for drinker?

parts.note: seems to be a book kept for a drinker, but means a large display book left on a low table where cups are put

explanation.surface: A book reserved for someone who drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A large illustrated book meant for browsing, displayed on a low table in a living room.

clue.text: Friendly government initially installed in African country

indicators.note: installed in places this letter inside the country

parts.note: Benin is a West African country

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word government

explanation.surface: A friendly government is put in power in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Benign means kind and gentle, well-disposed towards others.

clue.text: Ham finished? Then daughter must have egg

parts.note: over means finished, ended
an egg is O-shaped

explanation.surface: Is the ham done? Then the daughter needs an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: To ham is to overact, exaggerating a performance.

clue.text: Quickly flip over the page about little man

indicators.note: about says one piece goes round the other

parts.note: PTO stands for please turn over, written at the foot of a page
Ron is a short form of the man's name Ronald

explanation.surface: Someone is told to turn the page over fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Pronto is informal for at once, promptly, from Spanish.

clue.text: Kept away, being dispatched into a place of rest

indicators.note: into puts the dispatched letters inside the bed

parts.note: a bed is a place of rest
sent means dispatched, sent off

explanation.surface: Someone kept away by being packed off to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Absented oneself means stayed away, kept absent.

clue.text: Writer producing letters of note I collected

indicators.note: collected says the note's letters gather the I between them

parts.note: NB, nota bene, are the letters asking a reader to note something

explanation.surface: A writer produces notable letters, gathering them together.
explanation.definitionFit: A nib is a pen's writing point, standing for the pen.

clue.text: Blast from explosive — get away before that!

indicators.note: before puts the get away piece in front of the explosive

parts.note: scat is a command to go away
HE is short for high explosive

explanation.surface: A warning to flee before an explosive goes off.
explanation.definitionFit: To scathe is to attack harshly in words, a sense matching blast as criticise.

clue.text: Frenchman to straggle alongside English deserter

parts.note: Rene is a French man's name
to gad is to wander about aimlessly

explanation.surface: A Frenchman lags behind an English deserter.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade is someone who abandons a cause or party, a turncoat.
